name: Enable Game Mode
description: Turns on Windows Game Mode (Settings › Gaming › Game Mode).
mechanism: Writes AutoGameModeEnabled=1 under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\GameBar, the value behind the Settings toggle. When a game is detected Windows suppresses Windows Update driver installs and restart notifications and favours the game process over background work.
benefit: Fewer interruptions and less background work while playing; can improve frame-time consistency on systems with heavy background load.
drawback: Practically none on current Windows. Early Windows 10 builds (1703–1809) had stutter issues that have since been fixed.
evidence: Documented by Microsoft ('Use Game Mode while gaming on your Windows PC'). Average FPS gains are usually small; the main effect is fewer interruptions.

name: Disable background recording ("Record what happened")
description: Stops the Xbox Game Bar from continuously recording the last minutes of gameplay.
mechanism: Writes HistoricalCaptureEnabled=0 (Settings › Gaming › Captures › Record what happened). When on, gameplay is continuously encoded with the GPU video encoder and buffered to disk.
benefit: Removes continuous video encoding and disk writes during play. Typically a few percent FPS and lower frame-time variance, more on GPUs with limited encoder headroom.
drawback: You can no longer save a clip of something that already happened. Manual recording (Win+Alt+R) still works.
recommendedFor: Anyone who does not use instant replay from the Game Bar.
evidence: Settings › Gaming › Captures. Windows 10's own Settings page labelled this option 'Record in the background while I'm playing a game (this may affect game performance)'. Measured impact depends on the GPU's encoder.

name: Disable Game Bar game capture (Game DVR)
description: Turns off Xbox Game Bar game capture for this user.
mechanism: Sets GameDVR_Enabled=0 (HKCU\System\GameConfigStore) and AppCaptureEnabled=0 (HKCU\...\GameDVR). With capture off, the capture pipeline is not initialised when a game starts.
benefit: Removes capture hooks from games and prevents accidental recordings.
drawback: Game Bar recording and screenshots (Win+Alt+R / Win+Alt+PrtScn) stop working. Other recorders (OBS, NVIDIA App, AMD Software) are unaffected.
recommendedFor: Users who record with other software or not at all.
evidence: These are the per-user values Windows writes when capture is disabled in Settings; widely documented. Performance gain is small when background recording is already off.

name: Don't open Game Bar with the controller's Xbox button
description: Prevents the Xbox/Guide button on a controller from opening the Game Bar overlay.
mechanism: Writes UseNexusForGameBarEnabled=0 under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\GameBar (Settings › Gaming › Xbox Game Bar › 'Open Xbox Game Bar using this button on a controller').
benefit: Avoids accidental overlay pop-ups that steal focus mid-game.
drawback: The Game Bar must be opened with Win+G instead.
recommendedFor: Controller players who don't use the Game Bar.
evidence: Standard Settings toggle. No performance effect; convenience only.

name: Hide Game Bar startup tips
description: Stops the 'Press Win+G to open Game Bar' tip when games start.
benefit: Removes a notification that can appear over the game at launch.
recommendedFor: Everyone who finds the tip distracting.
evidence: Value written by the Game Bar's own settings. Convenience only.

name: Policy: disable Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting
description: Applies the Group Policy that disables Game Bar recording and broadcasting for every user.
mechanism: Sets AllowGameDVR=0 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\GameDVR (Administrative Templates › Windows Components › Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting).
benefit: Guarantees capture stays off for all accounts, even if a user re-enables it.
drawback: Affects all users; Settings shows 'managed by your organization'. Game Bar recording cannot be used at all.
recommendedFor: Shared or dedicated gaming PCs where recording is never wanted.

name: Enable optimizations for windowed games
description: Upgrades DirectX 10/11 games running windowed or borderless to the modern flip presentation model.
mechanism: Adds SwapEffectUpgradeEnable=1 to DirectXUserGlobalSettings (Settings › Display › Graphics › Default graphics settings). DWM can then use independent flip for legacy 'blt' model games.
benefit: Lower presentation latency in borderless/windowed games, and enables VRR and Auto HDR in windowed mode.
drawback: Rare game compatibility issues; it can be disabled per game in Settings › Display › Graphics.
recommendedFor: Players of DX10/11 games in borderless windowed mode.
evidence: Microsoft DirectX Developer Blog, 'Windowed game optimizations' (2022). Takes effect when the game next starts.

name: Enable Windows variable refresh rate for games
description: Lets DirectX 11 games without native VRR support use G-SYNC/FreeSync/Adaptive-Sync.
mechanism: Adds VRROptimizeEnable=1 to DirectXUserGlobalSettings (Settings › Display › Graphics › Variable refresh rate).
benefit: Tear-free presentation without V-Sync's added latency in more games.
drawback: Only works with a VRR-capable display, cable and driver; it does not replace enabling G-SYNC/FreeSync in the GPU control panel.
recommendedFor: PCs with a VRR (G-SYNC / FreeSync / Adaptive-Sync) monitor.
evidence: Microsoft documents the toggle ('Variable refresh rate' in Graphics settings, Windows 10 1903+). No effect when unsupported.
